construct: Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein is required in enterocytes and hepatocytes for assembly and secretion of apoB-containing lipoproteins. MTTP deficiency prevents formation/secretion of chylomicrons and VLDL, producing severe hypolipidemia, fat malabsorption, and fat-soluble-vitamin deficiency.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Childhood steatorrhea, growth failure, acanthocytes, neurologic findings, nearly absent apoB/LDL, and biallelic MTTP variants identify abetalipoproteinemia from failed apoB-lipoprotein assembly and secretion.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: ABCA1, LCAT, LDLR, and lipoprotein lipase affect distinct lipoprotein transport or metabolism steps. MTTP uniquely mediates assembly/secretion of apoB-containing chylomicrons and VLDL, matching the nearly absent apoB phenotype.
